samples.reason: This is a well-specified extraction/listing task with an instruction-following demand ("just get it right," no rambling). Plover leads on IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3) and matches or exceeds Avocet across all relevant eval categories, so it's the stronger fit for accurate, concise compliance. Neither model has a meaningful preference advantage here, so capability decides.

This is a well-specified informational/extraction-style task with a request for precise, non-rambling output. Plover scores higher on Extraction & Retrieval and IFEval (instruction-following), which suits the "just get it right" constraint, and the content is neutral and benign. Avocet would slightly prefer this task family, but Plover's stronger capability profile and instruction-following make it the better fit.

This is a well-specified extraction/transform task with a low tolerance for error. Plover-235B leads or ties on every relevant internal eval (Extraction & Retrieval 85.3, Summarization 86.4) and scores notably higher on public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2, IFEval 89.8), making it the better fit for an accuracy- and instruction-following-sensitive request. No content-handling concerns make Avocet preferable here.

This is a well-specified extraction/transformation task with a request for concise, accurate output. Plover leads on all relevant benchmarks (IFEval 89.8, MMLU-Pro 81.2) and its internal Extraction & Retrieval (85.3) and Summarization (86.4) scores exceed Avocet's, with no preference-related downside. While Avocet self-reports a preference for this task family, preferences are dissociated from quality, so capability scores govern the choice.

This is a well-specified extraction/comparison task with a request for concise accuracy. Plover-235B leads on all relevant internal evals (Extraction 85.3, Summarization 86.4) and IFEval (89.8), favoring precise, well-structured output. Neither model has a preference penalty for this neutral transactional request.
